items.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017
items.q: I worked with that man 18 years... And that’s how we worked down through the years.

ctx.x: Tell me about getting hooked up with Lionel Hampton.

Well now this was something, a left handed something. My friend, I had a friend, who’s a Charleston fellow, from Charleston, South Carolina. He was a trumpet player, a hell of a trumpet player. First chair trumpet player. And he was working in the band, in Lionel’s band, and he came to me one day, I was working at a club up in Harlem. He said, “Zeke” he said, “man, listen, this musician, he has an opening for a pianist. He needs a pianist.” He said, “Come on, man, come on down. I’ll come and pick you up tomorrow…

heard so many things about Hamp you know. And I just, I don’t know, I just felt I wouldn’t fit in there. He said, “Man, listen, leave it up to me. Let me take — .” He said, “I’ll tell you what, I’ll be here to pick you up tomorrow at 2:30.” And boy he was right there at 2:00 he was at my door. He drove me down to the rehearsal, 48th Street I think it was, I forget, that rehearsal studio. But anyway I went in and he said, “Hey Gates,” everybody was Gates. He said, “Come on and play one with me.” And the tune he…
